claim.qualifier: EPA combined-cycle range, Dual Max trim
claim.verbatim_quote: The dual-motor model we tested with the larger battery pack ('Max,' as Rivian calls it) has an EPA-estimated driving range of 410 miles.

sources.name: EPA fueleconomy.gov — 2025 Rivian R1S Dual Max

reality.qualifier: Consumer Reports 70 mph steady-state highway test on a 2025 R1S Dual Max purchased anonymously for $94,550. Recharged synthesis reports independent tests in the 330–350 mi range; CR's 358 is on the higher end of that distribution.
reality.verbatim_quote: Although it only managed 358 miles during our 70-mph highway-range test, that's still a pretty luxurious range.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — 2025 Rivian R1S Road Test Report
Recharged — 2025 Rivian R1S Range Test, synthesis of independent tests

narrative_one_liner: Rivian advertises 410 mi (R1S Dual Max); CR's 70 mph highway test measured 358 mi — 52-mile (13%) gap.
narrative: Rivian advertises 410 mi EPA range for the R1S Dual Max — the longest claim of any three-row electric SUV on sale. Consumer Reports' 70 mph highway test measured 358 mi. The 52-mile gap (12.7%) is one of the largest CR has documented across 26 tested EVs, tied with the Ford F-150 Lightning. EPA combined-cycle methodology consistently overstates highway range for heavy SUVs.
methodology_notes: Two Tier-2 sources converge: CR's instrumented test gives a single data point; Recharged synthesizes multiple independent tests showing 330–350 mi typical range, with CR's 358 mi at the upper end. Combined N=2+ independent measurements.
caveats: CR's tested unit was Dual Max with 22-inch wheels (per CR purchase note); EPA vehicle ID 48433 also documents Dual Max with 20-inch wheels at 410 mi. Wheel size affects range; the CR tested unit's wheels should be confirmed against the EPA-listed configuration.
The Dual Max trim represents the longest-range configuration; a buyer choosing the more popular Dual Large at 300 mi EPA would see a different gap.
Recharged's synthesis methodology is documented but represents an aggregator rather than a primary measurement source.
alternative_explanations: Three-row, 5,800+ lb SUV physics: highway aero drag dominates at 70+ mph. EPA cycle's lower average speed naturally favors EVs in this weight class disproportionately.
Battery degradation could affect older test units; CR's was a new purchase.
